title: Learning a Language for Real
summary: Ama and Carlos discuss why small daily habits beat long, rare study sessions.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: Ama and Carlos at a bright café table with notebooks, headphones and a small clock, no text

sentences.text: Carlos, I have been studying Italian for six months, but I feel I am not making progress.
How often do you practise?
Usually on Sunday. I study for about four hours, and then I do nothing for the rest of the week.
That might be the problem. Your memory needs repetition, not just one big effort.
But I thought long sessions were more efficient.
They feel productive, but you forget most of the material within a few days.
So you would recommend something shorter?
Yes, twenty minutes every day is far better than one marathon at the weekend.
It sounds almost too easy. Does it really make such a big difference?
In my experience it does, because the habit becomes automatic after a few weeks.
I suppose I could study while I drink my morning coffee.
Perfect. Link the new habit to something you already do every day.

quiz.explain: She studies for about four hours on Sunday and then does nothing.

sentences.text: There is another problem. I am afraid of speaking, because I make so many mistakes.
Everybody does, Ama. Mistakes are simply part of the process.
I know, but I get embarrassed when people correct me.
Try to see a correction as a free lesson rather than as a criticism.
That is a healthier attitude. I will try to remember it.
Also, find a conversation partner who is patient and curious.
Do you know any websites where I can meet language partners?
There are several. You can also join a local group that meets once a week.
Good idea. I would feel less nervous in front of a small group.
And keep a notebook with your favourite new expressions, then review them regularly.
I am already looking forward to my first conversation.
Remember to enjoy it. Motivation lasts longer when learning is fun.
